subject: Order form: escrow holdback & tax reserve — proposal and redlines
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: John Murray <jmurray@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Order form: escrow holdback & tax reserve — proposal and redlines

John — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I'm sending a proposed update to the Order Form (attached) and a summary of the commercial asks from Horizon so we can move to redlines and legal review. Key points from Redwood's side: 

- Escrow / holdback: our commercial team typically proposes a 10% holdback on first invoice tied to final acceptance for brand-new integrations.
- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net30 for self-serve & smaller deals, Net45 for signed enterprise orders where we provide additional credit terms.
- Invoicing entity: Redwood US (Redwood Inference, Inc.) will issue invoices unless Horizon requests an EMEA remittance path — please confirm.
- Taxes: need Horizon VAT registration certificate and confirmation whether Horizon expects reverse charge or withholding.

Attached: OrderForm_v3.docx (redline-ready) — please review and send formal redlines back to me and CC commercial/legal. I'll loop in our legal team once we have Horizon's redlines. 

Next steps: can Horizon confirm (a) PO will be issued to Redwood Inference, Inc., (b) VAT cert attached (if applicable), and (c) whether procurement can accept our 10% holdback or propose an alternative (bank guarantee/escrow agent)?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0193

[attachment: OrderForm_v3.docx (DOCX)]

From: John Murray <jmurray@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Analytics Legal <legal@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: escrow holdback & tax reserve — proposal and redlines

Kimberly — thanks for the note and the doc. A few items from procurement/legal side: 

- Holdback: 10% is higher than our standard. We can propose a 5% escrow holdback for the first 90 days post-acceptance, or alternatively, a performance bond/bank guarantee. Would Redwood accept 5% or require evidence that the escrow agent will release quickly on acceptance?
- Net terms: Horizon prefers Net45 on signed order forms. We can agree to Net30 if Redwood can provide a 30-day early-payment discount (TBD).
- VAT / taxes: attaching our VAT certificate. Horizon expects that VAT will be applied per EU rules; where reverse charge applies we'll mark it on the invoices.

Legal will circulate formal redlines to the Order Form later today; please have your legal team (cc'd?) review MSA-2025-44 references and the indemnity scope. We will also issue a PO once redlines are agreed.

Thanks,
John
John Murray
Head of Procurement | Horizon Analytics
jmurray@horizon-analytics.com
+1 212-555-0101

[attachment: Horizon_VAT_cert.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: internal: Horizon counter on escrow & netterms — suggested approach

Kim / Karthik — quick internal note after John's reply: 

- Escrow: We should avoid 10% if possible — it increases upfront cash strain. Proposed internal compromise: 7.5% holdback for first billing cycle, released after 60 days following documented acceptance milestones; OR accept 5% escrow if Horizon commits to a bank guarantee and earlier release. 
- Net terms: Leaning toward accepting Net45 for this deal given ARR and reference value, but ask for a small early-pay discount (1.5%) for Net30 option. 
- Entity & tax: Confirm remit to Redwood Inference, Inc. and accept reverse charge traces only when Horizon provides valid VAT cert (they supplied one). We should add language that any withholding taxes are Horizon's responsibility unless otherwise agreed. 

Action items for Kimberly: 1) Propose the 7.5% compromise with an explicit release schedule OR 5% + bank guarantee; 2) Ask legal to highlight MSA cross-references (MSA-2025-44) and ensure any holdback doesn't create unintended indemnity exposure. I've prepared a short redline summary (internal) attached. 

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

[attachment: redline_summary.xlsx (XLSX) — internal notes]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: John Murray <jmurray@horizon-analytics.com>, Horizon Analytics Legal <legal@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: escrow holdback & tax reserve — proposal and redlines

John / Legal team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the VAT cert. After internal review, Redwood can propose the following compromise to expedite contracting: 

Option A (preferred): 7.5% holdback on initial invoice, released in two tranches — 50% released after production sign-off and 50% released 60 days after sign-off. Holdback expires at renewal if acceptance criteria met. 

Option B (alternative): 5% escrow held by a mutually-agreed escrow agent for 60 days post-acceptance; Horizon to provide confirmation of bank guarantee if Redwood requests reduction of holdback. 

We can accept Net45 on the signed Order Form given the strategic nature of this deal, provided Horizon includes a PO referencing DEAL-1429-HZN. If Horizon chooses Net30 instead, Redwood requests a 1.5% early-pay credit applied to the first invoice. 

On taxes: Redwood will invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US). Where reverse charge applies, please confirm in writing per attached VAT cert; withholding taxes remain the customer's responsibility. 

I've attached an updated OrderForm_v3.docx for horizon legal to redline directly and added comments referencing MSA-2025-44 (see clause 4.2 and SOW acceptance language). Can your team return redlines by COB Friday so we can get legal aligned and route for signature? If that works, I'll ask our legal to prioritize review the moment we receive Horizon's redlines. 

DocuSign note: we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope once commercial terms are agreed. Link to sandbox envelope (for reference): https://app.docusign.com/DEMO/envelope/0a1b2c3d

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0193

[attachment: OrderForm_v3.docx (DOCX)]

From: John Murray <jmurray@horizon-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Order form: escrow holdback & tax reserve — proposal and redlines

Kimberly — thanks for the clear options. I'll escalate the two options with Legal & Finance this afternoon. Our preliminary view: Option B (5% escrow) + bank guarantee is likely to be acceptable to Finance, but Legal prefers to see release timings in the redline. We'll circulate formal redlines by Thursday COB and include a PO reference if all good. Appreciate the flexibility on Net45.

Will loop back once Legal sends their redlines.

Regards,
John
